key: Better than sovereignty over the earth, better than going to heaven, better than lordship over all worlds, is the reward of the first step in holiness.
s: The chapter on the world ends by setting one attainment above every kingdom and heaven; the Theravāda commentary, on verse 178, takes it as stream-entry, for a ruler of so much is not freed from hell, while the stream-enterer has shut the doors to woe.
src: The Theravāda commentary, Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā XIII.11 (on verse 178), the Pali, Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana edition (VRI), commit 60c7fb3 (2023)

opened.edition: Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana text, Vipassana Research Institute, s0502a.att.xml, commit 60c7fb3

evidence.words: Sotāpattiphalaṃ varanti yasmā ettake ṭhāne rajjaṃ kāretvāpi nirayādīhi amuttova hoti, sotāpanno pana pihitāpāyadvāro hutvā sabbadubbalopi aṭṭhame bhave na nibbattati, tasmā sotāpattiphalameva varaṃ uttamanti attho.
evidence.gloss: “The fruit of stream-entry is better”: because even one who has exercised rule over so great a domain is not freed from hell and the other lower states, whereas the stream-enterer, the doors to the states of woe shut, is not born an eighth time even if he is the weakest; therefore the fruit of stream-entry alone is better, highest. That is the meaning.
